Japanese: 戦闘勝利時、必ず宝箱を発見できる。
Target:

Guaranteed discovery of a treasure chest upon victory.

English: Those people control the monsters, make them act as extensions of their will... We judge this power a threat to the world, and will seal it away here.
Japanese: その民は、魔物を自在に操る。手足の如く己の意のままに……我々はこの力を世に仇なす脅威と判断し、ここに封印す。
Target:
那一族能随心驱使魔物，使其如臂使指……我们认定此力足以危害世间，故封印于此。
Those people control the monsters, make them act as extensions of their will... We judge this power a threat to the world, and will seal it away here.

English: They communicate with monsters. They need no special tools. I wish for this sight to become commonplace, and record it down here.
Japanese: その者は、魔物と心を通わす。特別な道具など必要とせず……ボクはこの光景が当たり前になることを願いここに記す。
Target:
此人能与魔物心意相通，无需任何特殊器具……愿有朝一日，这幅景象能成为寻常。我将它记于此处。
They communicate with monsters. They need no special tools. I wish for this sight to become commonplace, and record it down here.

English:
The girl dreams.
Of the outside world, glimpsed only in books.
Of all the many stars that fill up the night skies.
Japanese:
少女は夢を見る。
絵本で読んだ外の世界の。
夜空いっぱいに広がる満天の星達を。
Target:
少女做着梦。梦见书中才见过的外界，梦见铺满夜空的繁星。
The girl dreams.
Of the outside world, glimpsed only in books.
Of all the many stars that fill up the night skies.

English:
The girl dreams.
Of the village underground, stained in blood.
Of the sight of her family she was powerless to protect.
Japanese:
少女は夢を見る。
血に染まった地下の村の。
自分の無力で守れなかった家族の姿を。
Target:
少女做着梦。梦见血染的地下村落，梦见因自己无力而未能守住的家人。
The girl dreams.
Of the village underground, stained in blood.
Of the sight of her family she was powerless to protect.

English: Picked up as a child wandering the desert by soldiers. He was raised from that point on to bury his emotions and do his work dispassionately.
Japanese: 幼い頃、一人砂漠を彷徨っていたときに兵士に拾われた。それ以来、感情を殺しただ淡々と任務をこなすよう、教育を受けてきた。
Target:
幼时独自流浪沙漠，被士兵捡回。自此受训压抑感情，只知冷静执行任务。
Picked up as a child wandering the desert by soldiers. He was raised from that point on to bury his emotions and do his work dispassionately.

English: He's bad at expressing his emotions as a result, but he's still a boy. He thinks the sandskiff is the height of cool, and has been secretly delighted every time it's been modified.
Japanese: 故に、感情を表に出すのは苦手だが、まだまだ少年。砂船を最高にカッコイイと思っているし、改造の度に密かに心を躍らせていた。
Target:
因此他不善流露感情，但终究还是少年。觉得沙船帅得不得了，每次改装都暗自雀跃。
He's bad at expressing his emotions as a result, but he's still a boy. He thinks the sandskiff is the height of cool, and has been secretly delighted every time it's been modified.

English:
You're born into darkness.
You'll die in the darkness.
You're like me.
That's what I thought.
Japanese:
闇の中に生まれて。
闇の中で死んでいく。
君は僕に似ている。
そう思ったんだ。
Target:
生于黑暗，死于黑暗。你和我很像。我曾这样想。
You're born into darkness.
You'll die in the darkness.
You're like me.
That's what I thought.

English:
Took into the sun.
Taken into the light.
I broke your world.
My world is...
Japanese:
日の中に連れ出して。
光の中に連れ出された。
僕は君の世界を壊した。
君は僕の世界の……
Target:
把你带到阳光下。又被你带到光明中。我毁了你的世界。而你，是我世界的……
Took into the sun.
Taken into the light.
I broke your world.
My world is...

English: "Hey, Mom. Listen to this. I made some friends. Great friends, ones who talk to me a lot."
Japanese: 「ねぇ、お母さん、聞いてください。ボクに友人ができたんです。たくさんお喋りしてくれる、大切な友人ができたんです」
Target:
“妈妈，你听我说。我交到朋友了。很重要的朋友，他们愿意陪我说好多好多话。”
"Hey, Mom. Listen to this. I made some friends. Great friends, ones who talk to me a lot."

English: "Hey, Mom. Listen. I've decided to be a researcher. When I do that, you think you could talk to me a little?"
Japanese: 「ねぇ、おかあさん、聞いて。ボクもケンキュウシャになることにしたんだ。そうしたら少しは、おしゃべりしてくれるかな？」
Target:
“妈妈，你听我说。我决定也要当研究员。那样的话，你会不会愿意陪我多说几句话？”
"Hey, Mom. Listen. I've decided to be a researcher. When I do that, you think you could talk to me a little?"

English: The circus tamer girl is a hard worker, but she messes everything up. When she fails again today, the others will laugh it off.
Japanese: サーカスの猛獣使いの少女は、頑張り屋さんだけど失敗ばかり。今日も失敗しては、仲間達に「仕方ないなぁ」と笑われます。
Target:
马戏团的驯兽少女十分努力，却总是笨手笨脚。今天又闯了祸，伙伴们只会笑着说一句：“真拿你没办法。”
The circus tamer girl is a hard worker, but she messes everything up. When she fails again today, the others will laugh it off.

English: The girl with monster blood flowing within her was hated. Before she was picked up by the circus, the only thing ever directed at her was icy ridicule.
Japanese:
魔物の血が流れる少女は、
忌み嫌われていました。サーカスに拾われる以前、少女に向けられるのは冷たい嘲笑のみでした。
Target:
身怀魔物之血的少女一直遭人厌弃。被马戏团收留以前，迎接她的只有冰冷讥笑。
The girl with monster blood flowing within her was hated. Before she was picked up by the circus, the only thing ever directed at her was icy ridicule.

English:
No. 1
The monster's origins are unclear. There is too much we don't know about them. If we know our enemy better, perhaps we could find a path to harmony.
Japanese:
Ｎｏ．１
魔物の起源は明らかになっていない。私達は彼らについて知らないことが多すぎる。相手を知れば融和の道もあるかもしれないのに。
Target:
编号1
魔物起源至今不明。我们对它们所知太少。若能真正了解彼此，也许还有共存之路。
No. 1
The monster's origins are unclear. There is too much we don't know about them. If we know our enemy better, perhaps we could find a path to harmony.

English:
No. 2379
Humans were the biggest obstacle to my research. They cry about heresy and cast stones. Why? My research is correct, I'm sure of it. So why...?
Japanese:
Ｎｏ．２３７９
研究の最大の障害は人間だった。異端だと騒ぎ、石を投げる。どうして？私の研究は正しいはずだ。それなのにどうして……？
Target:
编号2379
研究最大的阻碍竟是人类。他们高喊异端，向我掷石。为什么？我的研究明明没有错。为什么……？
No. 2379
Humans were the biggest obstacle to my research. They cry about heresy and cast stones. Why? My research is correct, I'm sure of it. So why...?

English: Her specialty is steamed potatoes. She also likes sewing, and makes clothing for everyone in the village. She's got skills, as you can see.
Japanese: 得意料理はふかし芋。裁縫も好きで、村のみんなの服は彼女が仕立てている。腕前は見ての通り。
Target:
拿手菜是蒸土豆，也喜欢缝纫，村里众人的衣服都出自她手。手艺如何，一看便知。
Her specialty is steamed potatoes. She also likes sewing, and makes clothing for everyone in the village. She's got skills, as you can see.

English: Until she became pregnant with her daughter, she was the strongest warrior in the village. And those skills of hers can be seen in her daughter's strength, too.
Japanese: 娘を身ごもるまでは、村一番の戦士だったらしい。その腕前は、娘の強さからも窺い知れる。
Target:
据说怀上女儿以前，她是村中最强战士。女儿如今的身手，也足见母亲当年风采。
Until she became pregnant with her daughter, she was the strongest warrior in the village. And those skills of hers can be seen in her daughter's strength, too.

English: Aged men cloaked in ostentatious black robes. Their supercilious manner keeps others at arm's length—or farther. Their skill in the art of civics is nonetheless authentic.
Japanese: 仰々しい黒衣に身を包んだ老人達。彼らの傲岸な態度は、周りに人を寄せ付けない。政の腕は確かだというが……
Target:
一群身披夸张黑袍的老人。态度傲慢，令人敬而远之；但据说治政本领确有真材实料……
Aged men cloaked in ostentatious black robes. Their supercilious manner keeps others at arm's length—or farther. Their skill in the art of civics is nonetheless authentic.

English: These men once loved the same woman. Her dying wish was that the city would prosper, and as though taken by sorcery, that wish continues to bind the men to this day.
Japanese: 彼らはかつて同じ女を愛した男達だ。今は亡き女が最期に望んだのは街の繁栄。その願いはあたかも呪縛の如く、彼らを縛り続ける。
Target:
他们曾爱上同一名女子。女子临终只愿城镇繁荣。那遗愿仿佛咒缚，至今仍将众人紧紧束在一起。
These men once loved the same woman. Her dying wish was that the city would prosper, and as though taken by sorcery, that wish continues to bind the men to this day.

English: Taciturn soldiers clad in imposing armor. All who don it abandon the need for faces and names. They guard the city with coordinated vigilance.
Japanese: 立派な鎧に身を包む、寡黙な兵士達。その鎧を着た者には、もはや顔も名前も必要ない。今日も一糸乱れぬ統率で街を護る。
Target:
沉默寡言的士兵，身披威严铠甲。穿上它，脸与姓名便再无意义。众人步调如一，守卫着城镇。
Taciturn soldiers clad in imposing armor. All who don it abandon the need for faces and names. They guard the city with coordinated vigilance.

English: The soldiers have been together so long they know every scratch and nick on each other's armor. Though they know neither faces nor names, their bonds still run deep.
Japanese: 彼らは長い時間を共に過ごした。それは、鎧の傷の位置を自然と記憶するほどの時間だ。顔や名前を知らずとも、彼らの絆は深い。
Target:
他们并肩太久，久到连彼此铠甲上每道伤痕都熟记于心。纵不知面容姓名，情谊仍深。
The soldiers have been together so long they know every scratch and nick on each other's armor. Though they know neither faces nor names, their bonds still run deep.

English: This timid man once lacked confidence in his own circus troupe. That changed when he made the acquaintance of a white bird.
Japanese: 内気だった男はもともと、自らが経営するサーカス団にも自信が持てなかった。そんな彼が変わったのは、白い鳥と出会った頃。
Target:
这名内向男子曾连自己经营的马戏团都没有信心。直到遇见一只白鸟，一切才开始改变。
This timid man once lacked confidence in his own circus troupe. That changed when he made the acquaintance of a white bird.

English: The bird could speak, so to help build his confidence, he had it whisper, "My show is the greatest show in the world!" in his ear, over and over again.
Japanese: 自己暗示をかけるため、彼は人語を話す鳥に耳元で繰り返させた。「ウチノショーハスゴイゾ！」と、何度も、何度も。
Target:
那鸟会说人话。为了给自己壮胆，他让它一次又一次贴着耳边重复：“我们的表演天下第一！”
The bird could speak, so to help build his confidence, he had it whisper, "My show is the greatest show in the world!" in his ear, over and over again.

English: A man who wants to eliminate inequity and lift up the city's orphans. However, the reality is that his child's illness and the reactions of selfish adults have stopped him from seeing it done.
Japanese: 貧富の差を無くし、街の孤児をも救いたいと日々願う男。しかし、我が子の病気や我儘な大人達の対応で手が回っていないのが現実。
Target:
他想消弭贫富差距，也想救济城中孤儿。奈何自家孩子患病，加上任性的大人没完没了，他始终分身乏术。
A man who wants to eliminate inequity and lift up the city's orphans. However, the reality is that his child's illness and the reactions of selfish adults have stopped him from seeing it done.

English: The exhaustion he faces on the daily is making his hair fall out. When he walks the riverside, so much of his hair falls out and catches fire that he almost gets burned.
Japanese: 日々の気苦労は、着実に彼の毛根を蝕んでいる。彼が川べりを歩くと、抜け落ちた頭髪が燃え出し、火傷しそうになるほどだ。
Target:
日复一日的操劳正一点点侵蚀他的发根。沿河走上一圈，掉下来的头发甚至会烧起来，险些把本人烫伤。
The exhaustion he faces on the daily is making his hair fall out. When he walks the riverside, so much of his hair falls out and catches fire that he almost gets burned.

English: "Excuse me, traveler... Will you give us some food? ...No, I'm sure you wouldn't. I've never met a traveler who'd be so nice."
Japanese: 「旅人さん、ぼくらにごはんくれるの？……くれないよね。そんな優しい旅人さん、見たことないもん」
Target:
“旅行者……能分我们一点吃的吗？……不会吧。我从没见过这么好心的旅行者。”
"Excuse me, traveler... Will you give us some food? ...No, I'm sure you wouldn't. I've never met a traveler who'd be so nice."

English: "Those are some beautiful clothes you're wearing, traveler... Oh, I bet we could get so much good food to eat with the money from selling them..."
Japanese: 「旅人さん、きれいなお洋服きてるね。……それを売ったお金で、おいしいごはん、食べてみたいな……」
Target:
“旅行者，你穿得真漂亮……要是卖掉这些衣服，应该能换好多好多好吃的吧……”
"Those are some beautiful clothes you're wearing, traveler... Oh, I bet we could get so much good food to eat with the money from selling them..."

English: Born with the power of prophecy, I have a mission: to be a guiding light, that all might live without doubts in a world fraught with suffering.
Japanese: 預言の力を持って生まれた私には使命がある。それは苦しみばかりの世界でも皆が迷わずに生きていけるよう、輝く道標になること。
Target:
我生来拥有预言之力，也因此肩负使命：在苦难遍地的世界里化作明灯，让众人不再迷惘。
Born with the power of prophecy, I have a mission: to be a guiding light, that all might live without doubts in a world fraught with suffering.

English: I shall guide all to the proper path. I will give everything to fulfill my duty. So when we meet again someday, will you pat me on the head and tell me I did a good job, Father? Mother?
Japanese: 私は皆を正しく導きます。精一杯使命を果たします。だから、お父様、お母様。いつかまたお会いできた時は頭を撫でてくれますか。
Target:
我会引导众人走上正道，也会竭尽全力完成使命。所以父亲、母亲，若有朝一日还能相见，可以摸摸我的头，说我做得很好吗？
I shall guide all to the proper path. I will give everything to fulfill my duty. So when we meet again someday, will you pat me on the head and tell me I did a good job, Father? Mother?

English: I've been alone for ages, dears, and it makes me oh-so-happy to cook for someone. Go on now, eat up and make a dear old woman happy.
Japanese: ずっと一人だったから、誰かのために料理できることが嬉しいのさ。さあ、年寄りを喜ばせると思って、たんと食べておくれ。
Target:
“我一个人过了太久。如今还能为别人做饭，心里高兴得很。来，多吃点，就当哄老太婆开心。”
I've been alone for ages, dears, and it makes me oh-so-happy to cook for someone. Go on now, eat up and make a dear old woman happy.

English: My secret ingredients are frogs, lizards—ah, and juicy pit vipers! Come now, don't be shy! The decade or three of drying in the sun is where the flavor comes from!
Japanese: 料理の隠し味は、カエルにトカゲ、それからマムシ。ほらほら、遠慮しないで！どれもとっておきの、ウン十年物の干物だよ。
Target:
“秘方嘛，有青蛙、蜥蜴，还有蝮蛇！别客气，多吃点！这些可都是晒了几十年的上等干货。”
My secret ingredients are frogs, lizards—ah, and juicy pit vipers! Come now, don't be shy! The decade or three of drying in the sun is where the flavor comes from!

English: A pair of monsters who can change their appearance at will. They love to talk and are always laughing together. They also argue from time to time, but quickly make up.
Japanese: 姿を自在に変化させる、双子の魔物。お喋り好きで常に二人で笑いあっている。喧嘩をすることもあるようだが、すぐに仲直りする。
Target:
一对能随意变换外形的双生魔物。都爱说话，整日笑作一团；偶尔也会拌嘴，却总能很快和好。
A pair of monsters who can change their appearance at will. They love to talk and are always laughing together. They also argue from time to time, but quickly make up.

English: An ice monster that lived on the cliffs couldn't take the loneliness, and split itself into two. And as the two talked, they forgot which of themselves was the real one.
Japanese: 崖に棲む氷の魔物は孤独に耐えかね、自身を二つに分けた。そうしてお喋りするうちに、どちらが本当の姿か忘れてしまったようだ。
Target:
栖于悬崖的冰之魔物耐不住孤独，将自己一分为二。两边聊得太久，最后连谁才是真身都忘了。
An ice monster that lived on the cliffs couldn't take the loneliness, and split itself into two. And as the two talked, they forgot which of themselves was the real one.

English: An iron figure that does everything for humans: guidance, cleaning, cooking, you name it. It may turn out that it is not monsters that destroy humanity, but this sort of thing.
Japanese: 人間の代わりに、道案内、清掃、調理、なんでもこなす鉄の人形。人間を滅ぼすのは魔物ではなく、こういう存在なのかもしれない。
Target:
能替人类带路、打扫、做饭，几乎无所不能的钢铁人偶。将来毁灭人类的，也许不是魔物，而是这种东西。
An iron figure that does everything for humans: guidance, cleaning, cooking, you name it. It may turn out that it is not monsters that destroy humanity, but this sort of thing.

English: Now serves primarily as conversation for monsters. Likely it has functioned for so many years without breaking down because a monster is always repairing it.
Japanese: 今では専ら、魔物達の話し相手になっているようだ。長年壊れずに動き続けているのは、魔物が修理をしているからかもしれない。
Target:
如今它似乎主要负责陪魔物聊天。多年不坏，或许正因为总有魔物替它维修。
Now serves primarily as conversation for monsters. Likely it has functioned for so many years without breaking down because a monster is always repairing it.

English: A merchant who travels the world. He has a twin brother who runs a circus and is similarly well traveled.
Japanese: 世界各地を旅しながら、商売をする男。彼の双子の兄はサーカス団を経営しており、同じように様々な場所を回っていたらしい。
Target:
一名周游世界做买卖的商人。他有个经营马戏团的双胞胎兄长，同样四处奔波。
A merchant who travels the world. He has a twin brother who runs a circus and is similarly well traveled.

English: His ancestor was a legendary beast tamer who operated a carriage business. The twin brothers' world travels may very well be in their blood.
Japanese: 男の先祖は、「伝説の魔物使い」の足代わりの馬車屋だった。彼ら双子が世界各地を回るのは、その血の影響なのかもしれない。
Target:
其祖先曾是为“传说魔物使”代步的马车夫。兄弟俩走遍世界，或许正是受这份血脉影响。
His ancestor was a legendary beast tamer who operated a carriage business. The twin brothers' world travels may very well be in their blood.

English: This old man knows monsters. He can predict when and what kind of fiends will attack, hammers out strategies to deal with them, and then conveys them to the youngfolk.
Japanese: 老人は魔物に詳しい。次にいつどんな魔物が襲ってくるかを常に予想しており、その魔物に応じた作戦を考えて若者達に伝えている。
Target:
老人深谙魔物习性，总在预测下一次袭击何时发生、会来哪些魔物，再拟好对策传给年轻人。
This old man knows monsters. He can predict when and what kind of fiends will attack, hammers out strategies to deal with them, and then conveys them to the youngfolk.

English: The aged fellow also enjoys secretly betting with the old woman on what kind of and how many monsters will attack next—and it seems like he's picked up on a recent pattern...
Japanese: 老人は、次にどんな魔物が何匹やって来るか、村の老婆と賭けをして、密かに楽しんでいる。最近は傾向を掴んできた様子だが……
Target:
他还偷偷和村中老婆婆下注，猜下次会来什么魔物、来几只。最近似乎已经摸出了门道……
The aged fellow also enjoys secretly betting with the old woman on what kind of and how many monsters will attack next—and it seems like he's picked up on a recent pattern...

English: This elderly lady walks with a cane and acts like nothing bothers her, always greeting her fellow villagers with a bright smile.
Japanese: 老婆は常に杖をついて歩いているが、そんな事を気にさせないくらい、いつも変わらぬ笑顔で村の人々に明るく接している。
Target:
老婆婆总拄着杖，却从不显得衰弱。她始终带着灿烂笑容，爽朗地与村民打招呼。
This elderly lady walks with a cane and acts like nothing bothers her, always greeting her fellow villagers with a bright smile.

English: She's in exquisite health, and her legs aren't that bad. She uses the cane mostly to conserve her energy, in case monsters attack and she needs to flee by herself.
Japanese: 老婆は至って健康で足も悪くない。いざという時、一人で魔物から逃げられるよう、日々杖をつくことで体力を温存している。
Target:
其实她身体硬朗，腿脚也好。拄杖只是为了平日省些体力，真有魔物来袭时，好独自逃命。
She's in exquisite health, and her legs aren't that bad. She uses the cane mostly to conserve her energy, in case monsters attack and she needs to flee by herself.

English: This girl, who lost her sister to a monster when she was young, always looks so lonely in her corner of the village. She's friendly enough, though, and runs cheerfully over if called.
Japanese: 幼い頃魔物に姉を殺された彼女は、いつも寂しそうに村の片隅にいる。が、声をかければ明るく駆け寄ってくるくらいに人懐っこい。
Target:
幼时姐姐惨死于魔物之手。此后她总孤零零待在村角。不过性情亲人，只要有人招呼，便会笑着跑来。
This girl, who lost her sister to a monster when she was young, always looks so lonely in her corner of the village. She's friendly enough, though, and runs cheerfully over if called.

English: At some point after her sister was killed, she started calling everything that moves "big sister." Even, for example, the very monster which took her sister's life...
Japanese: 姉を殺された彼女はいつしか動くもの全てに「お姉ちゃん」と声をかけるようになった。たとえそれが姉を殺した魔物だとしても……
Target:
姐姐死后，她不知何时开始把一切会动的东西都叫“姐姐”。哪怕那正是杀死姐姐的魔物……
At some point after her sister was killed, she started calling everything that moves "big sister." Even, for example, the very monster which took her sister's life...

English: This young lad loves telling people he loves them. No matter their age or gender, all are subject to his loving confessions. Not a person in town has been spared his words of love.
Japanese: 彼は、すぐに愛の告白をする。年齢、性別問わずにどんどん愛の告白をする。村で彼からの告白を受けていない人はいないくらいだ。
Target:
这少年逢人便说“我爱你”。不分年龄性别，谁也逃不过他的告白；村里几乎无人没听过。
This young lad loves telling people he loves them. No matter their age or gender, all are subject to his loving confessions. Not a person in town has been spared his words of love.

English: This young lad loves telling people he loves them. He wants to make sure as many people as possible remember him, in case he ends up slaughtered by a marauding monster.
Japanese: 彼は、すぐに愛の告白をする。たとえ魔物に襲われ自分が死んでも、なるべく沢山の人達に自分の事を覚えておいてもらうために。
Target:
这少年逢人便说“我爱你”。他怕哪天死于魔物之手，便想让尽可能多的人记住自己。
This young lad loves telling people he loves them. He wants to make sure as many people as possible remember him, in case he ends up slaughtered by a marauding monster.

English: This man's obsession with his hair is—not to put too fine a point on it—hair-raising. Ever since childhood, he has meticulously trimmed his bangs every hour with sharp scissors.
Japanese: 男の髪型へのこだわりは常軌を逸している。幼い頃から切れ味抜群の鋏を使い、一時間おきに、寸分の狂いなく前髪を切り揃えた。
Target:
此人对发型的执着已近疯狂。自幼每隔一小时便拿锋利剪刀修齐刘海，分毫不差。
This man's obsession with his hair is—not to put too fine a point on it—hair-raising. Ever since childhood, he has meticulously trimmed his bangs every hour with sharp scissors.

English: One time, he accidentally snipped off part of a finger along with his bangs. Nonetheless, his careful coiffuring continues, with all nine-and-a-half of his remaining digits.
Japanese: 鋭利な鋏はある時、前髪に当てていた彼の指まで切り揃えてしまった。それでも彼は、短くなった指で丁寧に髪をセットし続ける。
Target:
有一次剪刘海时，他连手指也削去一截。即便如此，仍用剩下九根半手指细细整理头发。
One time, he accidentally snipped off part of a finger along with his bangs. Nonetheless, his careful coiffuring continues, with all nine-and-a-half of his remaining digits.

English: "Mistress's treats... Good..."
Japanese: 「ゴシュジンサマカラノゴホウビ……スキ……」
Target:
“主人给的奖励……喜欢……”
"Mistress's treats... Good..."

English: "Mistress's muscles. Look so tough. So good to chomp... Naughty, me. Let her hurt me. Could eat her. Anytime... Could eat now... Urgh..."
Japanese: 「ゴシュジンサマノカタクテタベゴタエアリソウナキンニク……イツデモクイコロセルオンナニシイタゲラレルハイトクカン……タベチャイソウ……ウウ……」
Target:
“主人那些硬邦邦、看着就很好咬的肌肉……明明随时都能吃掉她，却让她欺负我……好想吃……呜……”
"Mistress's muscles. Look so tough. So good to chomp... Naughty, me. Let her hurt me. Could eat her. Anytime... Could eat now... Urgh..."

English: There once was a girl who loved acrobatics. She practiced around the clock and took good care of her equipment. The moment when the audience burst into cheers was her greatest joy.
Japanese: 女は曲芸を愛していた。昼夜を問わず練習を重ね、公演に用いる道具の手入れを欠かさない。観客の声援が届く瞬間が最上の歓びだ。
Target:
曾有一名深爱杂技的女子。她日夜苦练，从不疏于保养道具。观众欢呼响起的那一刻，就是她最大的喜悦。
There once was a girl who loved acrobatics. She practiced around the clock and took good care of her equipment. The moment when the audience burst into cheers was her greatest joy.

English: This is not she, who loved the art more than any other. This is her daughter, who pushed her from up high and killed her to steal the lead role and the black uniform she'd always coveted.
Japanese: そんな誰より熱心だった女を、娘である彼女は高所から突き落として殺した。主役の座を奪うため、憧れの黒い衣装に身を包むため。
Target:
眼前并非那位最爱杂技的女子，而是她的女儿。为了抢走主角位置、穿上向往已久的黑色演出服，女儿从高处将母亲推下，夺走了她的命。
This is not she, who loved the art more than any other. This is her daughter, who pushed her from up high and killed her to steal the lead role and the black uniform she'd always coveted.

English: "Miss! Since I worked so hard at balancing on the ball, can I have a hug as a reward?!" cries a man cursed by a monster to look like a boy forever, as he approaches a woman after the show.
Japanese: 「お姉さん！玉乗り頑張ったご褒美に抱っこして！」魔物の呪いで見た目が子供のままの男は公演後、調子よく年頃の女性に近づく。
Target:
“姐姐！我这么努力练踩球，抱抱我当奖励嘛！”受魔物诅咒、外表永远停在少年时期的男人，演出结束后便这样凑到年轻女子身边。
"Miss! Since I worked so hard at balancing on the ball, can I have a hug as a reward?!" cries a man cursed by a monster to look like a boy forever, as he approaches a woman after the show.

English: He figures since he can't have a grown-up romance, this is the only way he'll ever enjoy a woman's touch. Ah, the days off with his monster companion are so long and lonesome...
Japanese: 彼は考えた。大人の恋愛ができないなら、女性と直に触れ合うにはそれしかないと。相棒の魔物と過ごす休日は長く寂しい。
Target:
反正无法谈成年人的恋爱，他便认定只有这样才能亲近女人。与魔物伙伴共度的休息日，实在漫长又寂寞……
He figures since he can't have a grown-up romance, this is the only way he'll ever enjoy a woman's touch. Ah, the days off with his monster companion are so long and lonesome...

English: A devout old man who adores the Lightfaith's fluffy-eared headwear. He is in fact quite convinced the fluffiness is the best part of the religion.
Japanese: 信心深い老人は、もふもふの耳がついた被り物に並々ならぬ愛を抱く。もふもふこそ、光の宗教の真骨頂であると確信しているのだ。
Target:
虔诚老人极爱光之信仰那顶带绒耳的头饰，甚至坚信“毛茸茸”才是整个信仰的精髓。
A devout old man who adores the Lightfaith's fluffy-eared headwear. He is in fact quite convinced the fluffiness is the best part of the religion.

English: His dearest wish was to see his beloved grandson wearing the fluffy ears. But with the lad having been killed by monsters, no amount of faith will make that wish come true.
Japanese: 魔物に命を奪われた愛する孫が、もふもふの耳を被る姿を見たかった。どれほど信仰を重ねても、その願いだけは永遠に叶わない。
Target:
他最大的愿望，是看心爱的孙子戴上那对绒耳。可孩子已死于魔物之手，再虔诚的信仰也换不回这份心愿。
His dearest wish was to see his beloved grandson wearing the fluffy ears. But with the lad having been killed by monsters, no amount of faith will make that wish come true.

English: A brilliant apothecary said to be able to heal any injury and cure any illness. One story even claims he sent the god of death fleeing with its chthonic tail between its legs.
Japanese: どんな怪我や病も治すと噂される凄腕の薬剤師。彼の前では死神も裸足で逃げ出す、という逸話がある。
Target:
医术高明的药剂师，据说任何伤病都能治好。甚至有传闻称，死神见了他也要落荒而逃。
A brilliant apothecary said to be able to heal any injury and cure any illness. One story even claims he sent the god of death fleeing with its chthonic tail between its legs.

English: The various cures he has concocted have saved many lives, but he still couldn't save his wife and daughter when they were dismembered by monsters.
Japanese: 彼が調合した薬は数多の命を助けた。だが魔物に四肢を切断された妻と娘を救うことはできなかった。
Target:
他调制的药救过无数性命，却没能救下被魔物肢解的妻子与女儿。
The various cures he has concocted have saved many lives, but he still couldn't save his wife and daughter when they were dismembered by monsters.

English: It was ten years ago that her son went out to defeat the monsters. Nonetheless, she prays every day that he yet lives.
Japanese: 彼女の息子が魔物を倒すと出て行ったのは、十年前のこと。それでも彼女は、毎日息子の生還を願い、祈りを捧げ続ける。
Target:
儿子外出讨伐魔物，已经十年。她仍每天祈祷，只盼孩子还活着。
It was ten years ago that her son went out to defeat the monsters. Nonetheless, she prays every day that he yet lives.

English: Her son couldn't bear his mother's overbearing love, and left home under the pretext of fighting monsters. These days, he evidently lives with his wife one town over.
Japanese: 彼女の息子は、母の深すぎる愛の重圧に耐えきれず、魔物との戦いを口実に家を出た。現在、息子は妻と隣町に暮らしているらしい。
Target:
其实儿子受不了母亲过于沉重的爱，借口讨伐魔物离家出走。如今似乎正和妻子住在邻镇。
Her son couldn't bear his mother's overbearing love, and left home under the pretext of fighting monsters. These days, he evidently lives with his wife one town over.

English: This woman's staunchly courteous manner makes it hard for her to fit in, and gives others a cold impression. She's a straight-laced lady, and isn't fond of revealing clothing.
Japanese: この女性は、振る舞いこそ折り目正しいが、周囲と馴染まず、冷たい印象を抱かせる。堅物で、人前で肌を見せることも好まない。
Target:
她举止一丝不苟，却总与周围格格不入，给人冷淡印象。性情古板，也不喜欢在人前袒露肌肤。
This woman's staunchly courteous manner makes it hard for her to fit in, and gives others a cold impression. She's a straight-laced lady, and isn't fond of revealing clothing.

English: She worries that being shy and anxious around others is why she cannot make friends in town. She constantly practices casual conversation in front of her mother's grave.
Japanese: 恥ずかしがり屋で人見知りな性格のために、街で友人ができないことが悩み。いつも母の墓前で、おしゃべりの練習をしている。
Target:
她苦恼于自己怕生害羞，始终交不到朋友。于是常在母亲墓前练习闲聊。
She worries that being shy and anxious around others is why she cannot make friends in town. She constantly practices casual conversation in front of her mother's grave.

English: I wish everyone could be happy. I wish everyone could live well forever. These are the wishes he makes with each fake flower he braids together.
Japanese: みんなが幸せでありますように。みんながいつまでも楽しく暮らせますように。そう願いながら偽物の花を一輪一輪、編んでいくよ。
Target:
愿大家都能幸福，愿大家永远快乐生活。怀着这样的愿望，他一朵一朵编起假花。
I wish everyone could be happy. I wish everyone could live well forever. These are the wishes he makes with each fake flower he braids together.

English: The flowers in his crown are made from monster hide. He wishes that one day he could make every monster in the world into a flower to decorate his hair with.
Japanese: 花冠に使う花は魔物の皮膚を使って作っているんだ。いつかこの世のすべての魔物を、花に変えて髪に飾れたらいいのに。
Target:
花冠上的花其实用魔物皮制成。他盼着有一天，把世上所有魔物都变成花，戴在自己头上。
The flowers in his crown are made from monster hide. He wishes that one day he could make every monster in the world into a flower to decorate his hair with.

English: Stricken with bedhead, shirt untucked—maybe this fellow's disheveled appearance is why he's so unpopular with others?
Japanese: 寝ぐせも直さないし、シャツもズボンからはみ出している。そんな風貌だからだろうか、彼は一部の仲間から人望がないようだ。
Target:
头发睡得乱翘，衬衫也没塞好。或许正因为这副邋遢模样，他在部分同伴中并不讨喜。
Stricken with bedhead, shirt untucked—maybe this fellow's disheveled appearance is why he's so unpopular with others?

English: Something about his untidy look and hapless smile seems to arouse a maternal instinct that makes him a hit with women. He's stolen away his fair share of lovers.
Japanese: だらしない恰好や頼りない笑顔は母性本能をくすぐるらしい。こう見えて女性にモテモテ。彼に恋人や妻を取られた男も少なくない。
Target:
可那不修边幅的样子和无害笑容似乎很能激起母性。别看这样，他其实颇受女人欢迎，被他抢走恋人或妻子的男人不在少数。
Something about his untidy look and hapless smile seems to arouse a maternal instinct that makes him a hit with women. He's stolen away his fair share of lovers.

English: An unmarried old woman who knows all the happenings of the City of Flame. Should she corner a fellow citizen, she'll treat them to an exhibition of her extensive knowledge.
Japanese: {CARDNAME:91350}のあらゆる事象に精通した、独り身の老婆。街の人間達を捕まえては、口うるさく自らの知識を披露している。
Target:
独身老婆婆对{CARDNAME:91350}大小事务了如指掌。每逮到一个城里人，便要絮絮叨叨展示自己的博闻强识。
An unmarried old woman who knows all the happenings of the City of Flame. Should she corner a fellow citizen, she'll treat them to an exhibition of her extensive knowledge.

English: People tend to give the chatty old woman a wide berth, but she has wisely changed her approach. By conveying the air of a knowledgeable person, she tempts travelers into speaking with her.
Japanese: そのやかましさに人々は彼女を遠ざけたが、老婆は賢く作戦を変える。知的な雰囲気を醸し出し、旅の者に声をかけさせるのだ。
Target:
众人嫌她太吵，总躲着走。老婆婆却聪明地换了招数：摆出学识渊博的气派，引得旅人主动搭话。
People tend to give the chatty old woman a wide berth, but she has wisely changed her approach. By conveying the air of a knowledgeable person, she tempts travelers into speaking with her.

English: This man evidently used to make a living slaying monsters, but injured his leg and retired. Since doing so, he has led a comfortable life, cane clutched in hand.
Japanese: 彼は元々、魔物退治を生業にしていたらしい。足を負傷し引退してからは、杖を片手に悠々自適の生活を送っている。
Target:
据说他原以讨伐魔物为生，后来伤了腿才退隐。此后拄着手杖，过起悠然自得的日子。
This man evidently used to make a living slaying monsters, but injured his leg and retired. Since doing so, he has led a comfortable life, cane clutched in hand.

English: Countless adventuring lives were spared in the wake of his retirement, as he was wont to kill competing hunters so he could keep all the monster-slaying profits to himself.
Japanese: 男の引退後、多くの冒険者の命が救われた。男は魔物退治の報酬を独占する為、競合相手の冒険者達を殺して回っていたのだ。
Target:
他退隐后，反倒救了无数冒险者。原来此人为了独吞讨伐报酬，过去常把同行猎人一并杀掉。
Countless adventuring lives were spared in the wake of his retirement, as he was wont to kill competing hunters so he could keep all the monster-slaying profits to himself.

English: This woman loves to hear tales of adventure from travelers. Her interest in them grew and grew until she opened the inn, where she can now hear heart-pounding stories all the time.
Japanese: 彼女は旅人の話す冒険譚が好きでした。趣味が高じて{CARDNAME:103020}を開き、その結果たくさんの心躍る物語を聞くことができたのです。
Target:
她最爱听旅人讲冒险故事，兴趣愈发浓厚，索性开了{CARDNAME:103020}。从此天天都能听到令人心潮澎湃的故事。
This woman loves to hear tales of adventure from travelers. Her interest in them grew and grew until she opened the inn, where she can now hear heart-pounding stories all the time.

English: As a matter of fact, she has painstakingly picked the best of those tales, and they'll be collected into a book! If you'd like to buy a copy, please send money to the following address...
Japanese: 今回その中から、彼女の厳選した至高の物語を一冊の本にまとめてご提供いたします。お求めをご希望の方は、こちらの宛先まで……
Target:
如今，她从无数故事中精挑细选，将其中佳作汇成一册！若想购买，请把钱寄到以下地址……
As a matter of fact, she has painstakingly picked the best of those tales, and they'll be collected into a book! If you'd like to buy a copy, please send money to the following address...

English: The owner of a weapon shop—and a sexy, deep voice. All he has to do is whisper a soft, "Buy it" into a window-shopper's ear, and they offer their wallets up as if in a trance.
Japanese: 低い美声が魅力的な{CARDNAME:103011}の店主。彼に「買いな」と耳元で囁かれるだけで、ひやかしの客もうっとりと財布を差し出してしまう。
Target:
{CARDNAME:103011}店主有一副迷人的低沉嗓音。只要贴在耳边轻声一句“买吧”，哪怕只是闲逛的客人也会恍惚着掏出钱包。
The owner of a weapon shop—and a sexy, deep voice. All he has to do is whisper a soft, "Buy it" into a window-shopper's ear, and they offer their wallets up as if in a trance.

English: In reality, he's just a hired employee managing the store, and he doesn't know thing one about weapons. He got the job because of his beefy physique, and, especially, that sexy voice.
Japanese: 実は彼は武器のことなど少しも知らない、雇われ店長だ。立派な体格と、なによりその美声を買われて、この職に就くことになった。
Target:
其实他只是受雇看店，对武器一窍不通。能当上店主，全凭魁梧身材——以及那副迷人的好嗓子。
In reality, he's just a hired employee managing the store, and he doesn't know thing one about weapons. He got the job because of his beefy physique, and, especially, that sexy voice.

English: In this cage behind me, you'll spy a selection of the finest monsters I collected as I tromped all over the land! Surely there must be one or two that a traveler like you fancies!
Japanese: この檻にはな、俺様が大陸を練り歩いて収集した、選りすぐりの魔物達がいるんだ。旅人さんが欲しい魔物もきっといるはずだぜ。
Target:
“我身后的笼子里，全是我走遍大陆才收来的上等魔物！像你这样的旅人，总有一两只看得上眼吧！”
In this cage behind me, you'll spy a selection of the finest monsters I collected as I tromped all over the land! Surely there must be one or two that a traveler like you fancies!

English: Hold on. I'm a human, you hear me? I just pretend to be a monster so I can catch them when they let their guard down. Make sure you don't attack me, even if you spot me out there!
Japanese: 待て、俺は人間だぞ？魔物のふりをして、油断したところを捕まえるんだ。俺を外で見かけても、くれぐれも攻撃しないでくれよな。
Target:
“等等，我可是人类！只是装成魔物，趁它们放松戒备再下手。以后在外面看见我，可千万别攻击！”
Hold on. I'm a human, you hear me? I just pretend to be a monster so I can catch them when they let their guard down. Make sure you don't attack me, even if you spot me out there!

English: Huh? You want me to tell you about myself? Well, I like apples, oranges, working at the shop, aaand my customers' smiling faces! I'm just an ordinary gal working at an item shop.
Japanese: え？私のことを教えてほしい？好きなものはリンゴとオレンジ。お店の仕事。お客さんの笑顔。{CARDNAME:103010}で働く、普通の女の子だよ。
Target:
“咦？想听我介绍自己？我喜欢苹果、橘子、在{CARDNAME:103010}工作——还有客人的笑脸！就是个普通店员啦。”
Huh? You want me to tell you about myself? Well, I like apples, oranges, working at the shop, aaand my customers' smiling faces! I'm just an ordinary gal working at an item shop.

English: You wanna know what I REALLY like? A cold one after work, sleeping in on days off...oh, and definitely customers who spend a LOT of money!
Japanese: 私が本当に好きなもの。仕事の後の一杯、お休みの日に寝坊すること、それから……たくさん買い物してくれるお客さんかな！
Target:
“真要问我最喜欢什么？下班后喝一杯，休息日睡懒觉……还有，当然是肯花大钱的客人！”
You wanna know what I REALLY like? A cold one after work, sleeping in on days off...oh, and definitely customers who spend a LOT of money!

English: I'm just an admirable, hardworking lad! Tireless, I daresay! I bust my hump on the daily! Customer service is my forte! Now come on in to paradise, and enjoy hours of fun!
Japanese: ボクは健気な勤労少年。疲れ知らずさ！毎日毎日せっせと働く。客あしらいもお手の物。魅惑の楽園、{CARDNAME:103013}をどうぞご贔屓に！
Target:
“我可是勤劳又懂事的少年，永远不知疲倦！天天卖力干活，招呼客人更不在话下。欢迎光临魅惑乐园——{CARDNAME:103013}！”
I'm just an admirable, hardworking lad! Tireless, I daresay! I bust my hump on the daily! Customer service is my forte! Now come on in to paradise, and enjoy hours of fun!

English: I saw my mom in a dream and woke up in tears. Augh! I'm not supposed to be like this. I'm a grown-up now. I have to work hard so I can feed my brother and sister!
Japanese: 夢の中で母ちゃんに会い、涙で目が覚めた。チクショウ！俺らしくもない。俺はもう大人なんだ。働いて働いて弟妹を食わせるんだ！
Target:
梦里见到母亲，醒来时满脸泪水。“可恶！这可不像我。我已经是大人了，得拼命干活，把弟弟妹妹养大！”
I saw my mom in a dream and woke up in tears. Augh! I'm not supposed to be like this. I'm a grown-up now. I have to work hard so I can feed my brother and sister!

English:
What thoughts does a
slime think? Has it the
capacity for intelligence
or emotion to begin
with? None are privy to
the goings-on inside
their gelatinous bodies.
Japanese: 何を考えているか、そもそも知性や感情があるのかもわからない、プヨプヨとした体を持つ謎の生き物。
Target:
史莱姆究竟在想什么？甚至有没有智慧和感情，都无人知晓。那团软胶般的身体里，藏着什么心思，谁也看不透。
What thoughts does a
slime think? Has it the
capacity for intelligence
or emotion to begin
with? None are privy to
the goings-on inside
their gelatinous bodies.

English:
Slimes are, in fact,
extremely sensitive
creatures who grieve each
and every last one of their
senselessly slaughtered
brethren. Naturally, they've
developed an innate hatred
for any and all adventurers.
Japanese: 実は、豊かな感受性を持っている。同胞がむやみに屠られることに嘆き、冒険者に怨嗟の念を向ける。
Target:
其实史莱姆感情极其细腻。眼看同胞无端遭到屠杀，它们悲痛不已，也因此本能地憎恨所有冒险者。
Slimes are, in fact,
extremely sensitive
creatures who grieve each
and every last one of their
senselessly slaughtered
brethren. Naturally, they've
developed an innate hatred
for any and all adventurers.

English: Isn't my purple form beautiful? I carefully control my diet to remain just the right shade!
Japanese: ぼくのからだ、紫色でキレイでしょう？毎日食べ物に気をつけて、この色をキープしてるんだ！
Target:
“我这一身紫色漂亮吧？为了保持最完美的色泽，我每天都很注意吃什么呢！”
Isn't my purple form beautiful? I carefully control my diet to remain just the right shade!

English: I killed my friend. It had to be done. They said green was prettier than purple! Can you believe that? Now, which do you like better?
Japanese: 友達を殺しちゃった。だって、紫より緑のほうがキレイだっていうんだもん。君は紫と緑、どっちが好き？
Target:
“我杀了朋友。没办法啊，谁叫它说绿色比紫色漂亮！你说，紫色和绿色哪个更好看？”
I killed my friend. It had to be done. They said green was prettier than purple! Can you believe that? Now, which do you like better?

English: These adorable furry critters are such a hit with children that plush animals of them are by far the best-selling souvenirs in town.
Japanese: そのもふもふした愛らしい容姿が、若者達のあいだで大人気の魔物。彼らを模したぬいぐるみは、町の土産屋の稼ぎ頭となっている。
Target:
毛茸茸又可爱的魔物，深受孩子们喜爱。以它们为原型的玩偶，更是镇上最畅销的伴手礼。
These adorable furry critters are such a hit with children that plush animals of them are by far the best-selling souvenirs in town.

English: The plush animals use real yeti fur, which has lead to a rise in live yetis attacking shops in attempts to recover their hideously altered brethren.
Japanese: ぬいぐるみには本物の毛が使われている。近頃、変わり果てた仲間を取り戻すため、土産屋を襲撃する個体が増えているという。
Target:
玩偶使用真正的雪人毛制作。近来，为夺回被做成怪样的同胞，活雪人袭击纪念品店的事件越来越多。
The plush animals use real yeti fur, which has lead to a rise in live yetis attacking shops in attempts to recover their hideously altered brethren.

English: Proto-yetis form herds of nine and diligently gather to practice striking a small ball with a metal bar.
Japanese:
この魔物は、９匹で群れを作る習性を持つ。
いつも皆で集まり、鉄の棒で小さな球を打つ練習に励んでいるようだ。
Target:
原始雪人习惯九只成群，
总聚在一起刻苦练习用铁棒击打小球。 Proto-yetis form herds of nine and diligently gather to practice striking a small ball with a metal bar.

English: They have a rigid hierarchy. Newcomers must fetch balls, and the leader will use the metal bar to beat to death any who are lax in this duty.
Japanese:
この魔物は、上下関係を非常に重んじる。
新入りはまず球拾いから。それを怠ると、リーダーに鉄の棒で撲殺される。
Target:
它们极重上下尊卑。新人先负责捡球；
若敢偷懒，首领就会用铁棒把它活活打死。 They have a rigid hierarchy. Newcomers must fetch balls, and the leader will use the metal bar to beat to death any who are lax in this duty.

English: A beast boasting soft hair with a bounce. Its locks protect its body from physical shock and, consequently, often protect its very life.
Japanese: 柔らかく弾力のある毛質が特徴の魔物。全身に生えた毛は衝撃を和らげる効果もあり、そのおかげで命拾いすることもしばしば。
Target:
全身长着柔软而富有弹性的毛。厚毛能缓冲冲击，也因此屡屡救它们一命。
A beast boasting soft hair with a bounce. Its locks protect its body from physical shock and, consequently, often protect its very life.

English: A furball is ever a ball of fur. This is quite convenient when it's cold, though more than a few perish from heat stroke when it's warm.
Japanese: いついかなるときも毛むくじゃらな魔物。寒い気候ではちょうどいいが、暑い気候になると、暑すぎて死ぬ個体もいるという。
Target:
毛球永远浑身是毛。寒冷时倒很舒服，一到炎热天气，却有不少会因中暑丧命。
A furball is ever a ball of fur. This is quite convenient when it's cold, though more than a few perish from heat stroke when it's warm.

English:
Their fur unkempt and
overgrown, these
functionally blind
creatures bite anything
they sense is moving,
in the hopes it
is edible.
Japanese: 伸びきった毛のせいで視界が悪く、前がほとんど見えていない。動く物の気配を頼りに齧りつき、それが食べられるかを確認する。
Target:
毛发杂乱疯长，几乎遮住全部视线。它们只要感觉到东西在动，便一口咬上去，先尝尝能不能吃。
Their fur unkempt and
overgrown, these
functionally blind
creatures bite anything
they sense is moving,
in the hopes it
is edible.

English:
As one might imagine,
biting anything that
moves, be it vicious or
poisonous, is a fine way
to cut your life short.
As a result, they are
nearing extinction.
Japanese: 凶暴な魔物や、毒性のある魔物にも構わず齧りつくため、そのほとんどが短命である。それ故に絶滅の危機に瀕している。
Target:
见什么动就咬，碰上凶暴或带毒的魔物也不例外，自然活不长。如今这个种族已濒临灭绝。
As one might imagine,
biting anything that
moves, be it vicious or
poisonous, is a fine way
to cut your life short.
As a result, they are
nearing extinction.

English:
Sword in paw, this proud
little beast will
challenge all comers to
a fair and honest duel,
and never back down,
regardless of their
opponent's size or
strength.
Japanese: 誇り高き小さな魔物。手にした剣に、清く正しく在ることを誓い、正々堂々と決闘に臨む。己より強大な敵にも怯むことはない。
Target:
小小身躯却极重荣誉，爪中握剑，发誓光明磊落。无论对手多么高大强壮，它都敢堂堂正正发起决斗。
Sword in paw, this proud
little beast will
challenge all comers to
a fair and honest duel,
and never back down,
regardless of their
opponent's size or
strength.

English:
Pure of mind though they
may be, their bodies are
in fact riddled with a
plague that, unbeknownst
to the poor creatures,
tends to be what
ultimately slays
their foes.
Japanese: 清い精神とは裏腹に、その体は雑菌に塗れている。決闘相手は剣にではなく、彼らが意図せず運ぶ疫病により命を奪われる。
Target:
心灵虽纯洁，身体却满是病菌。可怜的它们并不知道，许多对手最终并非死于剑下，而是死于它们无意传播的疫病。
Pure of mind though they
may be, their bodies are
in fact riddled with a
plague that, unbeknownst
to the poor creatures,
tends to be what
ultimately slays
their foes.

English: No point playing by the rules in this screwed-up world. We rats don't need pride, anyway! Live it up and make some noise!
Japanese: こんな狂った世界で真面目に生きるなんて虚しいだけだ。ドブネズミに誇りなんていらねぇ！馬鹿みたいに騒いで楽しく生きてやる！
Target:
“这种烂透的世界，守规矩又有什么用？下水道老鼠要什么尊严！闹个痛快，活得开心才算本事！”
No point playing by the rules in this screwed-up world. We rats don't need pride, anyway! Live it up and make some noise!

English: Truth is, I'd have loved to try playing by the rules. Live in a clean house. Eat hot meals. I hate the humans for making me feel like this.
Japanese: 本当は、真面目に生きてみたかった。清潔な家で暮らしてみたい。温かい料理を食べてみたい。こんな気持ちにさせる、人間が憎い。
Target:
“其实我也想好好过日子。住干净房子，吃热乎饭菜。是人类让我连这种念头都觉得可笑……我恨他们。”
Truth is, I'd have loved to try playing by the rules. Live in a clean house. Eat hot meals. I hate the humans for making me feel like this.

English: I picked up a real strong, sturdy hammer in the forest today. I can't wait to show it off to my friends!
Japanese: 今日森の奥で、すごく硬くて丈夫なハンマーを拾ったよ。えへへ、友達に見せびらかしてやろうっと！
Target:
“今天在森林深处捡到一把又硬又结实的锤子！嘿嘿，真想快点拿给朋友们炫耀！”
I picked up a real strong, sturdy hammer in the forest today. I can't wait to show it off to my friends!

English: Yep, this is how I'll get my revenge on all those bullies. Starting tomorrow I'll pay 'em a visit, one by one!
Japanese: これでやっと、ぼくを虐めたあいつやこいつに復讐できる。明日から一人ずつ、奴らを訪ねていこうっと！
Target:
“终于能向那些欺负过我的家伙报仇了。明天开始，一个一个找上门去！”
Yep, this is how I'll get my revenge on all those bullies. Starting tomorrow I'll pay 'em a visit, one by one!

English: Proficient with weapons and armor, these orcs strut around like they own the place in a show of strength to their fellows.
Japanese: 武器と防具の扱いに長けたその魔物は、同族達に自分の強さを誇示するかのように、我が物顔で棲み処を闊歩していた。
Target:
这种兽人擅长使用武器与防具，总在巢穴里横冲直撞，仿佛故意向同族炫耀自己的强大。
Proficient with weapons and armor, these orcs strut around like they own the place in a show of strength to their fellows.

English: Such arrogance often results in exile from their homelands. So they wander, aimless and alone, in search of a place to sleep.
Japanese: その魔物は、傍若無人な振る舞いのせいで、棲み処から追い出されてしまった。今日も一人、寝床を探して彷徨っている。
Target:
也正因如此蛮横，它们常被逐出巢穴。于是孤身漂泊，漫无目的地寻找下一处栖身之所。
Such arrogance often results in exile from their homelands. So they wander, aimless and alone, in search of a place to sleep.

English: Those massive stone axes are generational heirlooms. These beasts hunt down adventurers holding fast to memories of their ancestors.
Japanese: その魔物が持つ巨大な石斧は、先祖代々引き継がれている逸品だ。先代の思いを胸に、今日もまた冒険者を探しては襲い掛かる。
Target:
它们手中巨大的石斧，都是代代相传的珍品。怀着先辈留下的执念，今日仍在四处寻找冒险者下手。
Those massive stone axes are generational heirlooms. These beasts hunt down adventurers holding fast to memories of their ancestors.

English: Time after time, the adventurers prevail. The axes left behind are taken up by the next generation, whose hatred of humans only grows.
Japanese: その魔物は、今日もまた冒険者によって駆逐される。彼らが遺した石斧は、次の世代が回収し、人間への恨みを積み重ねていく……
Target:
可它们又一次败在冒险者手中。遗下的石斧会被下一代拾起，对人类的仇恨也随之越积越深……
Time after time, the adventurers prevail. The axes left behind are taken up by the next generation, whose hatred of humans only grows.

English: In combat, the bodies of these monsters rattle upon sighting an adventurer, almost as if they're laughing...
Japanese: 戦いの最中、その魔物は冒険者の傷を見て体中の骨をカタカタと鳴らす。まるで不気味に笑っているかのようだ。
Target:
战斗中，这种魔物一看见冒险者受伤，就会让全身骨头咔哒作响，仿佛在阴森地发笑……
In combat, the bodies of these monsters rattle upon sighting an adventurer, almost as if they're laughing...

English: Their bodies are made from the bones of humans they've killed. One can sometimes make out moans of the dead among the threatening rattle.
Japanese: 彼らの体は今まで殺した人間の骨で組み上げられている。威嚇のために鳴らすその骨からは、時折亡者の呻き声が混ざって聞こえる。
Target:
它们的身体由被自己杀死的人骨拼成。威吓时骨头咔哒作响，其中偶尔还夹着亡者呻吟。
Their bodies are made from the bones of humans they've killed. One can sometimes make out moans of the dead among the threatening rattle.

English: This monster appears with the vengeful spirit of its lover; their bond so powerful it leaves little vulnerability to attack.
Japanese: 恋人の怨霊と共に現れる魔物。彼らの連携は冒険者の付け入る隙が無いほどバッチリだという。
Target:
这种魔物会与恋人的怨灵一同现身。两者配合天衣无缝，几乎不给冒险者任何可乘之机。
This monster appears with the vengeful spirit of its lover; their bond so powerful it leaves little vulnerability to attack.

English: Sometimes they ignore their adventurer opponent to argue. Those lovers' quarrels are more vicious than any battle...
Japanese: 冒険者を無視して、恋人と痴話喧嘩を始めることがある。その様子は冒険者との戦闘よりも激しい……
Target:
它们有时会无视眼前冒险者，转头和恋人吵起来。那场痴情争吵，往往比真正战斗还要惨烈……
Sometimes they ignore their adventurer opponent to argue. Those lovers' quarrels are more vicious than any battle...

English: These monsters wear earmuff-like objects into battle, shake their bones in rhythmical beats, and launch up-tempo attacks.
Japanese: 彼らは戦いの際、必ず黒い耳あてのような物を身に付け、体を揺らし骨をリズミカルに鳴らしながら、テンポ良く攻撃をしてくる。
Target:
战斗时，它们总戴着黑色耳罩般的东西，随着节拍晃动骨骼，攻击也快得像踩着节奏。
These monsters wear earmuff-like objects into battle, shake their bones in rhythmical beats, and launch up-tempo attacks.

English: Listen closely, and you'll hear the crunching of bone, the rending of flesh, and cries of pain emanating from those black earmuffs.
Japanese: 戦闘中、彼らの黒い耳あてから漏れる音をよく聞いてみると、骨の砕ける音や肉の潰れる音、人間の悲鳴などが常に聞こえてくる。
Target:
若仔细听那黑色耳罩漏出的声音，会听见骨头碎裂、血肉碾烂，还有人类惨叫。
Listen closely, and you'll hear the crunching of bone, the rending of flesh, and cries of pain emanating from those black earmuffs.

English: We bare our fangs at the hubristic humans, so as to remind them they are little more than helpless prey.
Japanese:
我々は人間に牙をむく。
うぬぼれ屋の人間共は、思い出すだろう。人間とは愚かで力無き家畜に過ぎないということを。
Target:
“我们向傲慢的人类露出獠牙，只为让他们想起：自己不过是无力反抗的猎物。”
We bare our fangs at the hubristic humans, so as to remind them they are little more than helpless prey.

English: We love the arrogant humans, who will become our flesh and blood, and help us prosper. Wherever they try to flee, we will follow.
Japanese: 我々は人間を愛している。驕った人間共は、我々の血肉となり、種族に繁栄をもたらす。どこまで逃げようと、決して逃がしはせぬ。
Target:
“我们爱那些傲慢的人类。他们会化作我们的血肉，滋养族群繁盛。无论逃到哪里，我们都不会放过。”
We love the arrogant humans, who will become our flesh and blood, and help us prosper. Wherever they try to flee, we will follow.

English: These feral spirits attack silently from the shadows. Though their corporeal form is long gone, their bloodlust remains alive and well.
Japanese: 音もなく獲物の背後から襲い掛かる、獰猛な野獣の怨霊。肉体は朽ち果てても、血に飢えた野生の本能は健在である。
Target:
凶兽死后留下的怨灵，无声无息从阴影中扑向猎物。肉身虽早已腐朽，嗜血本能却丝毫未减。
These feral spirits attack silently from the shadows. Though their corporeal form is long gone, their bloodlust remains alive and well.

English: Though they make not a sound, they do have a faint scent. This means they prey mostly on humans, as animals with keener noses flee them.
Japanese: 音はしないが、微かな獣臭を放つ。そのため、嗅覚の鋭い動物達には逃げられてしまい、餌食となるのは人間くらいである。
Target:
它们不发一声，却残留淡淡兽腥。嗅觉敏锐的动物会早早逃开，于是最终沦为猎物的多半是人类。
Though they make not a sound, they do have a faint scent. This means they prey mostly on humans, as animals with keener noses flee them.

English: Though indeed slow on the ground, this creature can fly swiftly through the air. It is prized as a symbol of eternal youth.
Japanese: この魔物は足こそ遅いが、空を翔ける速さはなかなかのもの。不老長寿の象徴として尊ばれている。
Target:
这种生物在地面行动迟缓，飞上天空却快得惊人。人们将其视作长生不老的象征。
Though indeed slow on the ground, this creature can fly swiftly through the air. It is prized as a symbol of eternal youth.

English: The hardness of its shell is akin to steel. And yet, once flipped over onto said shell, it cannot right itself again.
Japanese: その甲羅は極めて硬く、鋼鉄に例えられるほど。ただし、ひっくり返ると自力では元に戻れない。
Target:
甲壳坚硬如钢。可一旦四脚朝天，就再也无法靠自己翻回来。
The hardness of its shell is akin to steel. And yet, once flipped over onto said shell, it cannot right itself again.

English: When withdrawn into its shell, this creature is often mistaken for valuable ore, resulting in many a severely burnt hand.
Japanese: 甲羅に手足を引っ込めていると、火山の鉱物に間違えられることがよくある亀の魔物。誤って触ると、大火傷を負うので要注意だ。
Target:
缩进壳里时，它常被误认成珍贵矿石。误触之人往往被烫得皮开肉绽，务必小心。
When withdrawn into its shell, this creature is often mistaken for valuable ore, resulting in many a severely burnt hand.

English: Armies venturing to colder climes take these creatures along for warmth. Apparently they also make great projectiles to hurl at enemies.
Japanese: 寒冷地に遠征する軍隊は、暖を取るために、この魔物を連れて行くという。敵に投げつければ、攻撃手段にもなると評判らしい。
Target:
远征寒地的军队会带上这种魔物取暖。据说扔向敌人还能当作威力不俗的投射武器。
Armies venturing to colder climes take these creatures along for warmth. Apparently they also make great projectiles to hurl at enemies.

English: In ancient times, these beasts' shells were used for divination. Priests heated them until they cracked, and read the resulting pattern.
Japanese: 古代の王朝では、この魔物の甲羅を使って占いを行った。神官が甲羅を焼き、現れたヒビで吉凶や天災の予兆を読んだという。
Target:
古代王朝曾用这种魔物的甲壳占卜。神官将壳烤裂，再从裂纹判断吉凶与天灾征兆。
In ancient times, these beasts' shells were used for divination. Priests heated them until they cracked, and read the resulting pattern.

English: The times changed, as did their exalted status. The once-mystical beasts are now treated as nothing more than seaside pests.
Japanese: 昔は神の使いとして珍重されていた彼ら。しかし時代と共に神秘性は失われ、浜辺で悪童に虐められるまでに成り下がってしまった。
Target:
昔日它们被奉为神使，备受珍视。时代变迁，神秘光环褪尽，如今甚至沦落到在海滩被顽童欺负。
The times changed, as did their exalted status. The once-mystical beasts are now treated as nothing more than seaside pests.

English: As winter approaches, small animals flock to the treants' hollows, seeking warmth. The treants happily oblige.
Japanese: 冬が近づくと、森中の小動物達が暖を求めてウロの周りに集まって来る。彼らはそれを優しく迎え入れる。
Target:
冬日将近，森林里的小动物会聚到树人空洞旁取暖。树人总温柔地将它们迎进去。
As winter approaches, small animals flock to the treants' hollows, seeking warmth. The treants happily oblige.

English: The poor creatures are frozen solid and added to a collection deep in the woods, which might even contain an adventurer or two...
Japanese: ウロに入った動物達は氷漬けにされ、森の奥深くにコレクションされる。そのなかには冒険者の姿も……
Target:
可怜的小动物随后被冻成冰块，收藏在森林深处。其中，似乎也夹着一两个冒险者……
The poor creatures are frozen solid and added to a collection deep in the woods, which might even contain an adventurer or two...

English: When these bashful creatures find a sweetheart, they slowly reach out and entwine them in their arms.
Japanese: 恥ずかしがり屋の彼女達は思い人を見つけると、植物の手をゆっくり伸ばして相手の体に絡みつく。
Target:
这些害羞的生物一旦遇见心上人，便会慢慢伸出植物般的手臂，将对方缠住。
When these bashful creatures find a sweetheart, they slowly reach out and entwine them in their arms.

English: They then absorb their life, bit by bit, until the object of their affection stirs no longer.
Japanese: そして彼らの鼓動が止まるまで、いつまでも、いつまでも、時間をかけて養分を吸い続けるのだ。
Target:
随后一点一点吸走生命，直到心上人的心跳彻底停止。它们会一直、一直吸下去。
They then absorb their life, bit by bit, until the object of their affection stirs no longer.

English:
Humans speak of
burning passion, but
rarely does that lead
to literal flames, as it
does with this creature.
Should any human
survive the flames, they
have a mate for life.
Japanese: 情熱的な彼女達は燃えるような恋をして、実際に熱く燃えあがる。その炎に耐えた者を生涯の伴侶とする。
Target:
人类常说“爱得火热”，对它们而言却是字面意义。坠入爱河时，全身会真的燃起来；若有人能熬过烈焰，便会成为它们终生伴侣。
Humans speak of
burning passion, but
rarely does that lead
to literal flames, as it
does with this creature.
Should any human
survive the flames, they
have a mate for life.

English:
In the unlikely event this
passion cools, their flame
disappears without a trace,
never to return again.
Japanese: 二人の愛が冷めてしまったとき、その炎は跡形もなく消え去る。そして二度と火が灯ることはない。
Target:
若这份爱意有朝一日冷却，火焰也会消失得无影无踪，并且永不再燃。
In the unlikely event this
passion cools, their flame
disappears without a trace,
never to return again.

English:
These sweet, gentle
creatures are infamous
for falling in love with
human men and giving
themselves over to them
out of a sense of love
deeper and more
profound than any lake.
Japanese: 可憐な姿をした彼女達は、しばしば人間の男と恋をする。そして、湖よりも深い愛情で相手に尽くす。
Target:
这些模样可爱、性情温柔的生物常爱上人类男子，并以深过湖底的情意全心奉献。
These sweet, gentle
creatures are infamous
for falling in love with
human men and giving
themselves over to them
out of a sense of love
deeper and more
profound than any lake.

English:
In return for their devotion,
they expect absolute
fidelity. Any man caught
being unfaithful is swiftly
pulled to the lake bed,
where his corpse may be
doted on for all time.
Japanese: 彼女達が浮気を許すことは決してない。深い深い湖の底に引きずり込み、その亡骸を生涯大切にする。
Target:
作为回报，它们要求绝对忠贞。若发现对方变心，便会把男人拖进深深湖底，此后终生珍爱那具尸体。
In return for their devotion,
they expect absolute
fidelity. Any man caught
being unfaithful is swiftly
pulled to the lake bed,
where his corpse may be
doted on for all time.

English:
Sparks quite literally fly
when these creatures
fall in love, but not out
of extreme passion. Nay,
these reserved creatures
merely want the objects
of their affection to take
notice of them.
Japanese: 彼女達は恋に落ちるとチカチカと電光を放つ。引っ込み思案なため、そうして意中の相手に気付いてもらおうとしているのだ。
Target:
它们坠入爱河时真的会电光四射，却不是因为热情奔放。恰恰相反，它们太过内向，只能靠闪光吸引心上人注意。
Sparks quite literally fly
when these creatures
fall in love, but not out
of extreme passion. Nay,
these reserved creatures
merely want the objects
of their affection to take
notice of them.

English:
Should they go unnoticed,
the sparks only grow in
intensity, ultimately ending
in lightning strikes that kill
many a thick-headed man.
Japanese: なかなか気付いてもらえないと電光の激しさが増していき、最終的には雷を落とす。鈍感な男には感電死が待っている。
Target:
若迟迟无人察觉，电光就会越来越强，最终化作落雷。迟钝的男人，往往只剩触电身亡一途。
Should they go unnoticed,
the sparks only grow in
intensity, ultimately ending
in lightning strikes that kill
many a thick-headed man.

English: My research leads me to believe the "fwip-fwip" sounds of these critters opening and closing their caps are a form of communication.
Japanese: 俺は魔物研究家。奴らは傘を器用に動かしてフゴフゴと音を出す。その音で、仲間と連携を取っているのではないかと俺は推測する。
Target:
“我是魔物研究者。我推测，它们灵巧开合菌盖发出的‘噗咕噗咕’声，是与同伴沟通的方式。”
My research leads me to believe the "fwip-fwip" sounds of these critters opening and closing their caps are a form of communication.

English: I've figured it out! The sounds are ceremonial atonement for killing their prey. Hm? Something's making a racket behind me...
Japanese: 長年の研究の末、俺はようやく突き止めた。あの音は獲物の命を奪うことへの贖罪の儀式だったのだ。ん？背後から何か音が……
Target:
“多年研究，我终于查明真相！那声音是夺走猎物性命后的赎罪仪式。嗯？背后怎么越来越吵……”
I've figured it out! The sounds are ceremonial atonement for killing their prey. Hm? Something's making a racket behind me...

English: Due to their mutated toxins, these monsters gleam in the sun. Their alluring glitter beguiles many an adventurer into eating them.
Japanese: 体に溜めた毒が、突然変異で光り輝くようになった魔物。その眩い輝きは冒険者を惑わせ、彼らを無意識に口元へと運ばせるという。
Target:
体内毒素发生异变，使它们在阳光下闪闪发亮。那迷人光泽会蛊惑冒险者，让人不知不觉把它们送进嘴里。
Due to their mutated toxins, these monsters gleam in the sun. Their alluring glitter beguiles many an adventurer into eating them.

English: Eating them induces vomiting. The glittering discharge further bewitches the poor adventurers into ending their own lives.
Japanese: 冒険者達は彼らを食したのち、猛毒により嘔吐する。そして輝く吐しゃ物を見た冒険者はさらに惑わされ、自ら命を絶ってしまう。
Target:
吃下后，冒险者会因猛毒剧烈呕吐。可那闪亮的呕吐物又会进一步迷惑他们，最终令其亲手结束生命。
Eating them induces vomiting. The glittering discharge further bewitches the poor adventurers into ending their own lives.

English: Wyverns kill any human they see. There is no escaping their flesh-rending talons, their bone-snapping jaws. It's a horrific way to go.
Japanese: 人間を見つけると、執拗に追い回し、いたぶり殺す。鋭いかぎ爪で肉を裂き、強靭な顎で骨を砕く。とにかく残忍で恐ろしい魔物だ。
Target:
翼龙见到人类便穷追猛打。利爪撕肉，强颚碎骨，直到把人活活折磨致死，残忍至极。
Wyverns kill any human they see. There is no escaping their flesh-rending talons, their bone-snapping jaws. It's a horrific way to go.

English: Wyverns were once friendly beasts. Only when humans began hunting them for equipment materials did they grow hateful.
Japanese: かつては人に友好的な種族であった。だが、装備の材料として乱獲されるようになってからは、人間を酷く恨むようになったという。
Target:
其实翼龙曾经亲近人类。直到人们为获取装备材料大肆捕猎，它们才开始深恨人类。
Wyverns were once friendly beasts. Only when humans began hunting them for equipment materials did they grow hateful.

English:
Long, long ago people
told stories of a
monster that would turn
into a prince if kissed
by a princess. It was
quite popular, and
survived for several
generations.
Japanese: 「お姫様が口づけをするとその魔物は、美しい王子の姿に変わりました」そんな物語を、遠い昔に人々が語り継いでいたと言います。
Target:
很久以前流传着一则故事：公主亲吻某种魔物后，它会化作俊美王子。这故事曾风靡一时，传了好几代。
Long, long ago people
told stories of a
monster that would turn
into a prince if kissed
by a princess. It was
quite popular, and
survived for several
generations.

English:
In retrospect, it was
likely the fact that
touching this creature—
let alone kissing it—
could poison you to
death that caused that
story to fall out
of favor.
Japanese: 実際は、その魔物に触れると毒で肌は爛れ、口づけなどしようものなら即死します。故に、その物語は廃れてしまったのでしょう。
Target:
后来人们大概终于想起，光是触碰这种魔物就可能中毒溃烂，更别提亲吻——那会当场毙命。故事也就渐渐没人讲了。
In retrospect, it was
likely the fact that
touching this creature—
let alone kissing it—
could poison you to
death that caused that
story to fall out
of favor.

English:
Shadow-black bodies,
Blood moons for eyes.
Joyous are their
  reveries,
Fangs seek a sanguine
  prize.
Japanese:
漆黒に溶ける身体。
赤く浮かぶ双月。
血に渇いた鋭き白。
響く歓喜の歌声。
Target:
身融漆黑，双月猩红。
白牙嗜血，欢歌回荡。 Shadow-black bodies, Blood moons for eyes. Joyous are their reveries, Fangs seek a sanguine prize.

English:
Slim fangs exsanguinate
Amidst a piercing
  scream.
Head lolls,
  pulse abates,
Consciousness
  a fading stream.
Japanese:
響く絶望の叫声。
突き立てられた白。
赤が奪われる器。
漆黒に溶ける意識。
Target:
绝望尖啸，白牙刺入。
赤红尽失，意识沉黑。 Slim fangs exsanguinate Amidst a piercing scream. Head lolls, pulse abates, Consciousness a fading stream.

English: This monster's in love! There's a beautiful toad in this odd box whom it hopes to see more of; for now, it watches the box as much as it can.
Japanese: 魔物は恋に落ちた。不思議な箱に映し出された、艶やかなメスの姿に。彼女の全てを見たいと願いながら、隙あらば箱を覗き込む。
Target:
这只魔物恋爱了。不思议的箱子里，有一只艳丽雌蟾令它魂牵梦萦。它只想看尽对方一切，一有空便盯着箱子。
This monster's in love! There's a beautiful toad in this odd box whom it hopes to see more of; for now, it watches the box as much as it can.

English: One day a human sliced into the box-toad's stomach. The lovesick monster was riveted. At last, it could see every last inch of the object of its affection.
Japanese: 箱の中の彼女は、ある日人間によって腹を切り裂かれた。その様子に魔物は釘付だ。彼女の全てを見ることができたのだから。
Target:
某天，人类剖开了箱中雌蟾的腹部。痴恋的魔物看得目不转睛——终于，它真的看见了心上人的“一切”。
One day a human sliced into the box-toad's stomach. The lovesick monster was riveted. At last, it could see every last inch of the object of its affection.

English: How I wish to see you, darling. Just one more time. If we should meet, I would profess my love to you.
Japanese:
会いたい。
もう一度、あの人に。
もし会えたのなら、
愛していると告げるんだ。
Target:
“好想见你。哪怕再见一次也好。若真能相逢，我一定要告诉你：我爱你。”
How I wish to see you, darling. Just one more time. If we should meet, I would profess my love to you.

English: I am grateful now, my darling, that you killed me. This way, I can love you for all eternity.
Japanese:
僕を殺してくれたことに、
いまでは感謝している。
これで永遠に君のことを
愛し続けられるのだから。
Target:
“如今我反而感谢你杀了我。这样一来，我就能永远爱着你了。”
I am grateful now, my darling, that you killed me. This way, I can love you for all eternity.

English: Turf wars among killer wasps are violent affairs. They trail opposing colony members to their nests and then attack with the thorns they hold.
Japanese: 殺人蜂の縄張り争いは激しい。別コロニーの同種を見つけると、追跡して巣を探し出す。そして手に持つ棘で攻撃をするのだ。
Target:
杀人蜂之间的领地争夺异常激烈。发现别群同类后，会一路跟踪找到巢穴，再用手中尖刺发动袭击。
Turf wars among killer wasps are violent affairs. They trail opposing colony members to their nests and then attack with the thorns they hold.

English: A horrific fate awaits the queen of the defeated colony. Eggs are laid upon her while she lives, so that her soft body shall nourish the larvae.
Japanese: 争いに敗れたコロニーの女王に待つのは、耐え難き苦難。栄養豊富で柔らかいその体は、生きながら卵を産み付けられる運命にある。
Target:
战败蜂群的女王将迎来可怕命运：仍活着时便被产下虫卵，柔软而营养丰富的身体会成为幼虫食粮。
A horrific fate awaits the queen of the defeated colony. Eggs are laid upon her while she lives, so that her soft body shall nourish the larvae.

English:
They call me a hero, but
I still fear these
three sounds: peals of
thunder, fluttering
insect wings, and tiny
tongues licking at their
jaws and mandibles.
Japanese: 雷が轟く音。虫の翅の音。舌なめずりの音。その三つの音が俺は怖い。村の英雄と持て囃されているが、奴らが怖くて仕方ないんだ。
Target:
“人们叫我英雄，可我最怕三种声音：雷鸣、虫翅振动，还有那小小舌头舔舐嘴边的声音。”
They call me a hero, but
I still fear these
three sounds: peals of
thunder, fluttering
insect wings, and tiny
tongues licking at their
jaws and mandibles.

English:
After paralyzing their
prey with lightning,
the awful, anticipatory
licking begins. Which
reminds me of the fourth
sound I fear—that of my
flesh being rent from my
body and devoured.
Japanese: 雷で獲物の自由を奪うと、奴らはご馳走を前に舌なめずりをした。あぁ、もう一つ追加だ……四つ目、己の肉が喰い千切られる音。
Target:
“它们先用雷电麻痹猎物，再开始令人发毛地舔嘴。对了，还得加第四种——自己的肉被撕下来、嚼碎吞下去的声音。”
After paralyzing their
prey with lightning,
the awful, anticipatory
licking begins. Which
reminds me of the fourth
sound I fear—that of my
flesh being rent from my
body and devoured.

English: If you're lost in a dark forest, beware of tiny red lights. They could be the flames of these vile, soul-sucking wasps.
Japanese: 暗い森で迷ったならば、小さな赤い光に気を付けろ。それは人の魂を啜ると言われる、恐ろしい悪魔の蜂が燃やす炎かもしれない。
Target:
若在黑暗森林中迷路，务必提防小小红光。那可能是恶魔蜂燃起的火焰——传说它们会啜饮人的灵魂。
If you're lost in a dark forest, beware of tiny red lights. They could be the flames of these vile, soul-sucking wasps.

English: It's said these wasps induce hallucinations of hope and despair in their captives. Agitated souls apparently make for a tastier meal.
Japanese: 奴らは捕らえた人間に、希望と絶望の幻覚を交互に見せるという。そうすることで魂が撹拌され、より美味になるらしい……
Target:
据说它们会让俘虏轮番看见希望与绝望的幻觉。被搅得越剧烈的灵魂，吃起来似乎越美味……
It's said these wasps induce hallucinations of hope and despair in their captives. Agitated souls apparently make for a tastier meal.

English: These monsters, skilled with magic, persisted in spiritual form upon death. They scare people by appearing in mirrors or along the waterfront.
Japanese: 魔術に長けた魔物が、死後に霊魂のみとなった姿。気まぐれに鏡の中や水辺に姿を映し、人間を驚かせる。
Target:
精通魔法的魔物死后，灵魂仍未消散。它们时而映在镜中，时而现身水边，专以惊吓人类取乐。
These monsters, skilled with magic, persisted in spiritual form upon death. They scare people by appearing in mirrors or along the waterfront.

English: Rumor has it these spirits, restless from existing so long after death, are researching magical methods of reincarnation.
Japanese: 長い長い死後の生活に退屈しており、どうにか生き返れないものかと、転生の魔術を研究しているらしい。
Target:
听说这些幽灵对漫长死后生活厌倦已久，正研究能让自己转生复活的魔法。
Rumor has it these spirits, restless from existing so long after death, are researching magical methods of reincarnation.

English:
That this creature
spends its days lazing
about in a stupor is a
testament to its nearly
uncontested spot atop
the monster hierarchy.
Japanese: 非常に温厚で普段はボーッと過ごしている。それは強さの証。彼らに危害を加えられる生き物が、ほとんど存在しないためである。
Target:
它平日总懒洋洋发呆，正说明它几乎稳坐魔物顶端——世上能真正伤到它的生物少之又少。
That this creature
spends its days lazing
about in a stupor is a
testament to its nearly
uncontested spot atop
the monster hierarchy.

English:
People often hunt the
younglings, lest they
mature. Ironically, it
is the smashing of these
hunters' fragile skulls
that teach the beasts
the joys of wanton
slaughter.
Japanese: 成長したら……それを恐れた人々は、まだ無垢である彼らに刃を向ける。それをへし折り頭蓋を砕くとき、彼らは殺戮の愉悦を知る。
Target:
人们害怕它长大，常趁幼年便动手猎杀。讽刺的是，正是在折断兵刃、砸碎猎人脆弱头骨时，它们第一次尝到了杀戮快感。
People often hunt the
younglings, lest they
mature. Ironically, it
is the smashing of these
hunters' fragile skulls
that teach the beasts
the joys of wanton
slaughter.

English: We will take from them. Their food, their land, their loved ones. We will take from them until they are eradicated.
Japanese: 我々ハ奴ラカラ奪ウ。食料モ土地モ、大切ナ存在モ。根絶ヤシニナルマデ、奪イ続ケテヤルノダ。
Target:
“我们要从他们手中夺走一切。食物、土地、挚爱之人。直到他们彻底灭绝，一样也不留下。”
We will take from them. Their food, their land, their loved ones. We will take from them until they are eradicated.

English: We will take from them. Their food, their land, their loved ones. We have to, before they do the same to us.
Japanese: 奴ラハ我々カラ奪ウ。食料モ土地モ、大切ナ存在モ。ダカラ、奪ワレル前ニ奪ワナケレバナラナイノダ。
Target:
“他们会夺走我们的食物、土地、挚爱之人。所以在被夺走以前，我们只能先下手。”
We will take from them. Their food, their land, their loved ones. We have to, before they do the same to us.

English: The troll's boundless appetite is such that one could eat an entire village's worth of humans and still feel hungry afterward.
Japanese: 人を食らう恐ろしい魔物。その胃袋は底なしだ。人間が住む村を丸ごとひとつ食らい尽くしてもなお、お腹を鳴らしている。
Target:
这种食人魔胃口深不见底。哪怕把整座村庄的人吃个精光，肚子照样咕咕作响。
The troll's boundless appetite is such that one could eat an entire village's worth of humans and still feel hungry afterward.

English: Human-fed troll flesh is considered a delicacy, though hunting the beasts tends to provide more food for the trolls than humans.
Japanese: 人を食べた彼らの肉は、珍味として美食家達に愛されている。しかし、彼らを捕獲するために命を落とす狩猟者が後を絶たない。
Target:
吃过人肉的食人魔，据说肉质堪称珍馐。只是前去捕猎的人，往往反倒成了它们更多的口粮。
Human-fed troll flesh is considered a delicacy, though hunting the beasts tends to provide more food for the trolls than humans.

English: トロルB（傷アリ）_表
Japanese: トロルB（傷アリ）_表
Target: トロルB（傷アリ）_表

English: トロルB（傷アリ）_裏
Japanese: トロルB（傷アリ）_裏
Target: トロルB（傷アリ）_裏

English: The box this monster carries with it is incredibly cold inside, which is likely how it preserves its prey.
Japanese: この魔物が大事そうに持っている箱の中は、常に低温で保たれている。狩った獲物を新鮮な状態で保存しておくためであろう。
Target:
它珍重抱着的箱子内部始终冰冷，想来是为了让猎物保持新鲜。
The box this monster carries with it is incredibly cold inside, which is likely how it preserves its prey.

English: Alas, it generally eats its prey the instant it kills it, meaning its box is always empty. Which poses the question, why carry it at all?
Japanese: 捕らえた獲物は、その場ですべて食い尽くすため、箱の中は常に空っぽ。一体何のために箱を持っているのか、よく分からない。
Target:
可它通常刚捕到猎物就当场吃光，箱子永远空空如也。既然如此，为何还要随身带着？
Alas, it generally eats its prey the instant it kills it, meaning its box is always empty. Which poses the question, why carry it at all?

English: Those figures on church drain spouts were once monsters that terrorized humans. Eventually they came to be seen as guardians of the church.
Japanese: 教会の外壁を伝う雨樋達。あれは遠い昔、人間を襲う魔物を封印した姿だった。長らく、彼らは教会の守り神だと思われていた。
Target:
教堂排水口那些雕像，其实是远古时袭击人类的魔物被封印后的模样。久而久之，人们反倒把它们当成教堂守护神。
Those figures on church drain spouts were once monsters that terrorized humans. Eventually they came to be seen as guardians of the church.

English: Though the spell that sealed them away was broken long ago, they've forgotten who they are. Would they'd forgotten their bloodlust, too...
Japanese: 実は封印などとっくの昔に解けていたが、彼らは自分が何者だったのかすら忘れていた。人間を殺したいという欲求を除いて……
Target:
其实封印早已解除，只是它们连自己原本是谁都忘了。可惜，想杀人的冲动却没忘……
Though the spell that sealed them away was broken long ago, they've forgotten who they are. Would they'd forgotten their bloodlust, too...

English: A master sculptor found a crumbling statue in front of a church and restored it to utterly lifelike glory.
Japanese: とある天才彫刻家が、古びた教会に佇む壊れた石像を修復した。彼によって直された石像は、まるで生きているかのようだった。
Target:
一位天才雕刻家发现教堂前破损的石像，便将其修复。修好后的石像栩栩如生，仿佛真有生命。
A master sculptor found a crumbling statue in front of a church and restored it to utterly lifelike glory.

English: Something bad has possessed the statue, perhaps due to its fearsome visage. Now it needs no repairs, for it heals itself quick as a blink.
Japanese: そのあまりにおぞましい見た目のせいか、石像によくない何かが憑依した。今では修復も必要ない。いつの間にか直っているから……
Target:
也许因为模样太过骇人，某种不祥之物附上了石像。如今已不需再修，因为不知何时，它总会自行复原……
Something bad has possessed the statue, perhaps due to its fearsome visage. Now it needs no repairs, for it heals itself quick as a blink.

English: The proto-gargoyle is quite fond of its staff with a yellow plate attached to it. It gives its gray body a splash of color and character.
Japanese: その黄色い板のついた棒を魔物はとても気に入っている。灰色で染まった体の中で、鮮やかな色は彼に個性を与えてくれた。
Target:
这只原始石像鬼非常喜欢那根挂着黄色牌子的棒子。灰扑扑的身体里，那抹鲜黄给了它独一份个性。
The proto-gargoyle is quite fond of its staff with a yellow plate attached to it. It gives its gray body a splash of color and character.

English: Being adorned in beautiful yellow makes it so happy it could die. Eager to show it off, it shoves its sign in the face of every passerby.
Japanese: 美しい黄色を身に着けることが嬉しくてたまらない魔物。通りかかる生き物すべてに見てほしくて、その板を相手の顔に押し付ける。
Target:
能披上漂亮黄色，它高兴得简直要死。为了向所有人炫耀，见到路过生物就把牌子往对方脸上怼。
Being adorned in beautiful yellow makes it so happy it could die. Eager to show it off, it shoves its sign in the face of every passerby.

English: A temptress called the Queen Ashwing lives deep in the forest. The powdery scales she spreads about enthrall humans whom she takes to her nest.
Japanese: 深い森の奥。灰羽の女王と呼ばれる魔物がいる。その魔物は鱗粉を振り撒いて人間を魅了し、巣に囚えてしまうという。
Target:
森林深处住着一只被称为“灰羽女王”的妖艳魔物。它散出的鳞粉会魅惑人类，再将其带回巢穴。
A temptress called the Queen Ashwing lives deep in the forest. The powdery scales she spreads about enthrall humans whom she takes to her nest.

English: Troubled is the queen. The scales her wings shed never cease to captivate humans. Today, too, must she gather food for more hungry mouths to feed.
Japanese: 女王は悩んだ。羽ばたく度に出る鱗粉で、人を魅了してしまうことを。女王は巣に来た人を養うため、今日も食糧を集めている。
Target:
女王却为此烦恼不已。每次振翅落下的鳞粉都会迷住人类。为了养活来到巢里的那些人，她今天也得外出寻找食物。
Troubled is the queen. The scales her wings shed never cease to captivate humans. Today, too, must she gather food for more hungry mouths to feed.

English: Legend has it that keeping one of this creature's golden antennae in your wallet or coin purse brings good luck.
Japanese: その魔物の黄金に輝く触角を財布に入れてお守りにすると、幸福になれるという言い伝えがある。
Target:
传说将这种魔物闪着金光的触角放进钱包，就能带来好运。
Legend has it that keeping one of this creature's golden antennae in your wallet or coin purse brings good luck.

English: Monsters whose antennae have been stolen sink to the dark seabed, where they hum hexes as they die in obscurity.
Japanese: 触角を奪われた個体は暗い海の底に身を隠す。そして呪いの唄を口ずさみ、人知れずに死んでいく。
Target:
失去触角的个体会沉入昏暗海底，低声哼唱诅咒之歌，然后无人知晓地死去。
Monsters whose antennae have been stolen sink to the dark seabed, where they hum hexes as they die in obscurity.

English: A just creature is a protector of the weak, keeper of the peace, friend to nature, and ruthless slayer of evildoers.
Japanese: それは正義を行使する者。弱きを助け、平和を護りし者。自然を愛し生きる、悪を決して赦さぬ者。
Target:
所谓正义，应是扶危济弱、守护和平、亲近自然，并毫不留情地诛灭恶徒。
A just creature is a protector of the weak, keeper of the peace, friend to nature, and ruthless slayer of evildoers.

English: At least, that is how I would define it. But what constitutes a just creature to the monsters? Humans have no way of knowing.
Japanese: それは己にとっての正義を行使する者。魔物にとっての正義など、人間には分かりようもない。
Target:
至少，这是人类眼中的正义。至于魔物心中的正义究竟是什么，人类无从知晓。
At least, that is how I would define it. But what constitutes a just creature to the monsters? Humans have no way of knowing.

English: There once was an old woman who picked up a mysterious rock. Warm to the touch, she took a great liking to it and brought it home with her.
Japanese: ある老婆が神秘的な石を拾いました。触れるとほんのり温かいその石を、老婆は大層気に入って、家に持ち帰ることにします。
Target:
从前有位老婆婆捡到一块神秘石头。石头摸起来微微发暖，她喜欢得不得了，便带回了家。
There once was an old woman who picked up a mysterious rock. Warm to the touch, she took a great liking to it and brought it home with her.

English: From the rock emerged a blackened creature, its shrieks capable of ending life. But the old woman was quite deaf, and they lived happily ever after.
Japanese: 石から黒い生物が現れ、命を奪う叫びをあげました。しかし、耳が遠い老婆には聞こえず、二人は末永く暮らしましたとさ。
Target:
石中钻出一只漆黑生物，尖叫声足以夺人性命。幸好老婆婆耳背，什么也没听见，于是一人一怪从此幸福生活在一起。
From the rock emerged a blackened creature, its shrieks capable of ending life. But the old woman was quite deaf, and they lived happily ever after.

English: This fiend inhabits roadside pebbles, diving into the orifices of passersby. Those caught unawares inevitably breathe their last.
Japanese: 道端の小石の中に潜み、通る者の虚を突いて襲いかかる魔物。不意を突かれた者は、為す術もなく、命を奪われてしまうという。
Target:
这种魔物藏在路边小石里，趁行人不备钻入身体孔窍。毫无防备的人往往来不及反抗，便一命呜呼。
This fiend inhabits roadside pebbles, diving into the orifices of passersby. Those caught unawares inevitably breathe their last.

English: In fact a skittish creature, it secludes itself in rocks out of sheer anxiety. The surprise of someone passing by drives it from one hiding spot to another.
Japanese: 実はこの魔物、極度のビビリ症で引きこもり。普段は石の中で静かに暮らしているが、人が近づくと驚いて飛び出てしまうという。
Target:
其实它胆小得要命，只因过度不安才躲进石头。有人经过时反而会吓得冲出来，再慌忙寻找下一个藏身处。
In fact a skittish creature, it secludes itself in rocks out of sheer anxiety. The surprise of someone passing by drives it from one hiding spot to another.

English: Aberrants all must die. Must be wiped out at any cost, before WE are.
Japanese: 異形ハ一匹残ラズ殺サナケレバナラナイ。我々ガ滅ブ前ニ、何トシテモ駆逐シナケレバナラナイ。
Target:
“异形必须一只不剩地杀光。趁我们尚未灭亡，不惜一切代价也要将它们彻底驱逐。”
Aberrants all must die. Must be wiped out at any cost, before WE are.

English: This why we monsters were born. This why we monsters gave up humanity.
Japanese: 我々魔物ハ、ソノタメニ生ミダサレタノダカラ。我々魔物ハ、ソノタメニ人間ヲヤメタノダカラ。
Target:
“我们魔物正是为此而生。我们也正是为此舍弃了人类身份。”
This why we monsters were born. This why we monsters gave up humanity.

English: More repulsive than a monster. Less merciful than one. Detached, they do naught but devour civilization.
Japanese: それは、魔物よりもおぞましく、魔物よりも慈悲を持たぬ。ただ淡々と文明を食らい尽くすのだ。
Target:
它比魔物更可怖，比魔物更无慈悲。毫无情感，只会冷冷吞噬文明。
More repulsive than a monster. Less merciful than one. Detached, they do naught but devour civilization.

English: They are aberrants. A living weapon made by humans to kill humans. Slaughterers without emotion.
Japanese: その名は異形。人間を殺すために人間に生み出された生きた兵器。感情を持たぬ殺戮者。
Target:
其名为“异形”。人类为了杀死人类而制造的活体兵器，没有感情的屠戮者。
They are aberrants. A living weapon made by humans to kill humans. Slaughterers without emotion.

English:
Generations spent
underground have
atrophied their senses
such that only taste
remains. Naturally,
they devour all
they encounter.
Japanese: 長い地中での生活により、視覚、嗅覚、聴覚を失い、触覚すらも退化した魔物。彼らは唯一残された味覚を頼りに、暴食を続ける。
Target:
长期生活地下，使它们失去视觉、嗅觉、听觉，连触觉也逐渐退化，只剩味觉。因此见什么便吞什么。
Generations spent
underground have
atrophied their senses
such that only taste
remains. Naturally,
they devour all
they encounter.

English:
How else would you have
them survive? Imagine
living in a world of
darkness and silence;
your sense of taste the
only thing that reminds
you you're still alive.
Japanese: 彼らにはそうするより他ないのだ。味覚以外を失った暗黒の世界では、味を感じ続けることだけが、生を実感する手段なのだから。
Target:
除此之外，它们还能怎样活下去？在那无光无声的世界里，唯有不断尝到滋味，才能确认自己仍活着。
How else would you have
them survive? Imagine
living in a world of
darkness and silence;
your sense of taste the
only thing that reminds
you you're still alive.

English: "Why do they bother me? I just want to sleep in peace. I just want to sleep quietly here in this mountain where I don't get in anyone's way."
Japanese: 「ドウシテ、彼ラハ邪魔ヲスル？我ハ静カニ寝タイダケナノニ。誰ノ邪魔ニモナラヌヨウ、コノ山デヒッソリ寝タイダケナノニ」
Target:
“为何总有人来打扰？我只想安静睡觉。只想躲在这座山里，不妨碍任何人，静静睡下去。”
"Why do they bother me? I just want to sleep in peace. I just want to sleep quietly here in this mountain where I don't get in anyone's way."

English: "Study, study, study! {CARDNAME:1051} always bugs me to do it every single day! But I don't wanna study! Nothing makes me happier than a nice relaxing nap!"
Japanese: 「勉強勉強！{CARDNAME:1051}は毎日、口煩く勉強しろと言う。でも僕は勉強なんかしたくない。ゆっくりお昼寝することが、僕の幸せなんだ」
Target:
“学习、学习、还是学习！{CARDNAME:1051}每天都唠叨个不停。可我才不想学！舒舒服服睡个午觉，才是最幸福的事！”
"Study, study, study! {CARDNAME:1051} always bugs me to do it every single day! But I don't wanna study! Nothing makes me happier than a nice relaxing nap!"

English: "I'm sooo hungry, but it'd be so mean to eat them. I have to hold back... I should be able to avoid them if I stay here where nothing grows."
Japanese: 「腹ガ減ッテ仕方ガナイ。ダガ、彼ラヲ食スノハアマリニモ酷。我慢セネバ……草木モ生エヌココナラバ、彼ラヲ避ケラレルハズダ」
Target:
“饿得难受……可把他们吃掉实在太残忍。必须忍住……这里寸草不生，待在这里应该就能避开他们。”
"I'm sooo hungry, but it'd be so mean to eat them. I have to hold back... I should be able to avoid them if I stay here where nothing grows."

English: "The pie you used to make me was sooo good! Like the best in the world! So please, {CARDNAME:1051}... Come back. Make it for me again..."
Japanese: 「{CARDNAME:1051}が作ってくれたパイは最高さ！世界一おいしいんだ！だからさ、お願いだよ……帰ってきてよ。また作ってよ……」
Target:
“{CARDNAME:1051}做的派最好吃了，天下第一！所以求你了……回来吧。再给我做一次……”
"The pie you used to make me was sooo good! Like the best in the world! So please, {CARDNAME:1051}... Come back. Make it for me again..."

English: "My cliffs are impenetrable. Fall, and be flattened below. The crimson blossoms that bloom on the white snow will surely be beautiful."
Japanese: 「我ガ守ルコノ崖ハ、難攻不落。落チテペチャンコニナッテシマエ。真ッ白ナ雪ノ上ニ咲ク赤イ花ハ、サゾカシ美シイダロウ」
Target:
“我守的悬崖固若金汤。掉下去摔成肉饼吧。洁白雪地上绽开的猩红花朵，一定很美。”
"My cliffs are impenetrable. Fall, and be flattened below. The crimson blossoms that bloom on the white snow will surely be beautiful."

English: "I dream of wearing a dress made by my brother and going to a show. But I like red and white both, it's hard to choose. Which does {CARDNAME:1051} like?"
Japanese: 「お兄ちゃんが作ったドレスを着て、ショーに出るのが私の夢。白いのもいいし赤いのも捨てがたい。{CARDNAME:1051}はどっちが良いと思う？」
Target:
“穿上哥哥做的礼服登台，是我的梦想。白色很好，红色也舍不得。{CARDNAME:1051}觉得哪种更漂亮？”
"I dream of wearing a dress made by my brother and going to a show. But I like red and white both, it's hard to choose. Which does {CARDNAME:1051} like?"

编号2841

Ｎｏ．５１５８

编号5158

No. 5158
I was right about the monsters. I was right! I have to continue with my research. If I fail, please take care of the rest... My dearest.

English: A beast sealed beneath the earth. Though dim its consciousness grew over the many moons, its intent to save the world remained strong.
Japanese: 地下に封印された魔物。長い月日を経て、自我が曖昧になっているが、世界を救済するという意志だけは強く残されている。
Target:
被封印在地下的魔物。漫长岁月令它意识日渐模糊，唯独“拯救世界”这份意志依旧无比坚定。
A beast sealed beneath the earth. Though dim its consciousness grew over the many moons, its intent to save the world remained strong.

English: To protect those he holds dear... To save the world... He chose to become a beast, all the while expecting he would be put to the sword by the lives he saved.
Japanese: 大切な存在を守るため。この世界を救うため。男は魔物になることを選んだ。紡いだ命に、いつか刃を向けられると予感しながら……
Target:
为了守护珍爱之人，为了拯救世界，他选择化身魔物。即便早已预感，总有一天会被自己救下的生命举刃相向……
To protect those he holds dear... To save the world... He chose to become a beast, all the while expecting he would be put to the sword by the lives he saved.
